newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - Sonae Ind 96 profit seen higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Sonae Ind 96 profit seen higher.

text.p: Portuguese analysts have revised upward their profit forecasts for wood products concern Sonae Industria because of improved market conditions and a fall in interest rates.

Analysts say the company, part of the Sonae Investimentos group, should post net profit for 1996 of between 400 and 700 million escudos compared with the firm's own forecast which was at the bottom end of that scale.

"The results have improved not because prices have risen but because they have not fallen as we thought they would," said Rosa Cunha, of ESR-Espirito Santo Research, which now foresees profit of 560 million escudos compared with an initial forecast of 400 million.
"The fall in interest rates which was bigger than expected also improved (Sonae's) financial situation," she added.
Sonae Industria has said its sales for this year will be steady at 64 billion escudos.
Joao Leandro of Lisbon brokers M.Valores believes profit will be just 400 million this year, but has revised his 1997 outlook up to 1.6 billion escudos from 800 million.
Leandro based his revision on Sonae Industria's new integrated management with Tafisa, which he said had saved on the cost of primary materials.
He said a new factory in Brazil, which is due to start production in 1998, would provide strong growth potential.

"Sonae's forecasts (for 1996) were relatively conservative. It is well known that the relocation of its production will have a positive impact on results," said Jose Carlos Tomas of Banco Portugues de Investimento (BPI).
Sonae has already begun to prepare for its production move by shutting down some centres in Portugal.

Diego Ortega of brokers Midas forecasts net profit after minority interests of 650 million escudos for 1996 as Sonae reaps the benefits of its switch from wood agglomerates to MDF-Medium Density Fibre.
"Sonae will continue with the reorganising of its companies, separating wood agglomerates from the MDF," BPI's Tomas said.
The world market production capacity for wood agglomerates is 100 million cubic metres, while MDF capacity is 18 million cubic metres.
Leandro of M.Valores said a forecast six percent in home sales this year would also create new outlets for Sonae Industria's products.
"There is usually a time lapse of between six and nine months between home sales and their impact on the furniture markets," he said.
